targetText:
This article will express our views on guerrilla warfare and its correct
utilization. Above all, we must emphasize at the outset that this form of
struggle is a means to an end. That end, essential and inevitable for any
revolutionary, is the conquest of political power.
summary: Guerrilla warfare is not an end in itself, but an instrument for the revolutionary conquest of political power.
explanation: Guerrilla fighting is neither a romantic adventure nor a self-sufficient military objective. It is a specific political method of armed struggle employed by an oppressed people to destroy the repressive state apparatus of the ruling class and establish revolutionary workers and peasants power.
context: Written in September 1963 for Cuba Socialista following the 1959 victory of the Cuban Revolution, addressing debates among Latin American communist parties over armed struggle versus peaceful electoral paths.
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

targetText:
The subjective conditions in each country, the factors of revolutionary
consciousness, organization and leadership, can accelerate or delay
revolution, depending on the state of their development. Sooner or
later in each historic epoch objective conditions ripen, consciousness
is acquired, organization is achieved, leadership arises, and revolution
takes place.
summary: Subjective conditions of leadership and organization determine whether maturing objective crises erupt into successful revolution.
explanation: While extreme exploitation and economic crises provide the objective basis for revolution, they do not automatically produce revolutionary change. A dedicated political-military vanguard must actively develop subjective consciousness and organize the masses to seize historical opportunities.
context: Reflects the core premise of foco theory: that a committed revolutionary nucleus can help create the subjective conditions for revolution rather than waiting passively for crisis conditions to spontaneously organize themselves.

targetText:
In the present historical conditions of Latin America, the national
bourgeoisie cannot lead the ant feudal and anti-imperialist struggle.
Experience demonstrates that in our nations this class : even when
its interests clash with those of Yankee imperialism : has been
incapable of confronting imperialism, paralyzed by fear of social
revolution and frightened by the clamor of the exploited masses.
summary: The Latin American national bourgeoisie cannot lead anti-imperialist liberation because fear of the working masses binds it to imperialism.
explanation: Unlike the progressive European bourgeoisie of the 18th century, the dependent capitalist classes of the Global South are deeply intertwined with landed oligarchs and foreign imperialist capital. Terrified of popular social revolution from below, the national bourgeoisie inevitably capitulates to imperialism rather than leading genuine national emancipation.
context: Written in the context of the Alliance for Progress and reformist illusions among Latin American bourgeois parties in the early 1960s.

targetText:
As Fidel has said, the cordillera of the Andes will be the Sierra Maestra
of Latin America; and the immense territories this continent encompasses
will become the scene of a life or death struggle against imperialism.
summary: Anti-imperialist liberation in the Americas is continental in scope, demanding international solidarity across borders.
explanation: Because United States imperialism operates across national boundaries to coordinate military interventions and prop up military dictatorships throughout the hemisphere, individual national revolutions cannot remain isolated. The liberation of Latin America demands coordinated continental solidarity and anti-imperialist struggle.
context: Echoes the Second Declaration of Havana (1962), forecasting the continental spread of national liberation movements across the Andes and Central America.
